records.source_span: I was chatting with David again today about keyboard setups. David mentioned he actually keeps his own Gboard keyboard height on short because he has smaller hands and prefers the keys closer together. He said he tried medium and tall but always went back to short.

On my phone I switched to Gboard as my default input method around March 3rd this year. I'd been using SwiftKey before that for over a year, but it became unbearably laggy after an update and I was really frustrated about losing all my customized autocorrect entries.

When I first set up Gboard back in early March, I started with the default medium keyboard height setting. I also set the theme to a plain dark gray background because I really can't stand those flashy gradient themes — they feel cluttered and distracting. I turned off the emoji suggestions bar at the top to get more screen space for the actual text area.
I also set the theme to a plain dark gray background because I really can't stand those flashy gradient themes — they feel cluttered and distracting.
I turned off the emoji suggestions bar at the top to get more screen space for the actual text area.

I bumped the keyboard height up to tall around mid-March because I kept hitting the wrong keys with my big thumbs. The medium setting just felt too cramped at the time. The tall setting gave me a bit more room between keys and I was making fewer typos for a while. I remember being pretty happy with that change initially.

I switched the keyboard height back down to medium about a week ago and honestly it feels way better now. I noticed I was actually mistyping more with the tall setting lately, probably because my thumbs had to stretch further to reach certain keys at the top of the keyboard. The medium height puts everything in a more comfortable range. So right now it's back on medium and I'm planning to keep it there.

I added Japanese as a secondary input language in Gboard around the second week of April for my casual Japanese study. The globe key lets me toggle between English and Japanese, which is really convenient. I've been practicing hiragana and some basic kanji, and having it right on my phone keyboard makes it easy to look things up quickly while studying.
I added Japanese as a secondary input language in Gboard around the second week of April for my casual Japanese study.

I set that up on April 1st specifically because I started a Spanish conversation exchange with a coworker named Elena. We meet every Thursday at lunch. So I needed to type characters like ñ and accented vowels regularly, and the US International layout handles that really well with dead keys.
